However, if geopolitical tensions in the Middle East diminish, India's economic growth prospects could enhance.
title: Is AI putting Indian IT jobs at risk? What Moody’s says about the future of work

author: DHRUV YADAV
description: India is focusing on the security of military equipment by investigating component origins and assembly processes. The government has implemented restrictions on importing components from adversarial countries like China since 2020. Additionally, new frameworks for assessing security vulnerabilities in drones are being established through Army Design Bureau initiatives. The AASHVAST laboratories will conduct thorough checks of drone hardware and software for potential risks.
title: India's new defence battle: Rooting out Chinese tech from its weapons

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: Ted Turner's family is set to auction 20 exquisite paintings by renowned 19th-century American artists, aiming to benefit the Turner Foundation. This collection, showcasing breathtaking landscapes of the American West, carries both cultural and financial significance. The auction, planned for January 2027, underscores Turner's commitment to philanthropy and environmental causes, with proceeds directed towards conservation projects that preserve vital natural habitats.
title: Ted Turner's Montana paintings head to $20m auction to benefit conservation

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Samuel L. Jackson and LaTanya Richardson Jackson received the Clarence and Jacqueline Avant HollyRod Humanitarian Award at a charity gala. The event recognized their humanitarian efforts and contributions to supporting families affected by autism and Parkinson's disease. Hosted by Holly Robinson Peete and Rodney Peete, the gala focused on raising funds and awareness for the challenges these families face.
title: Samuel L Jackson and wife honoured by charity helping over 50,000 families

author: TOI
description: India's employment landscape is undergoing a fundamental shift. The opportunity lies in ensuring that employees are equipped to work effectively with these tools. As AI adoption deepens, organisations will need to focus not just on technology deployment but also on helping their workforce understand, adopt and use these capabilities responsibly.
title: AI, talent gaps and labour reforms: Forces redefining India's employment landscape

author: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI
description: The 45-year-old's departure comes after several days of uncertainty over his future, with United already working on appointing Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement.
title: Michael Carrick sacked as Manchester United head coach as turmoil deepens

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: An 11-month-old infant named Koah Sharp was discovered alive after being buried in a dog crate. His father, Michael Comer, has been charged with attempted murder after the search lasted for 24 hours. Rescuers found Koah underground, which helped him survive due to cool temperatures and an air pocket. Authorities were alerted when his grandmother reported him missing shortly after she left him with his father.
title: Baby buried in dog crate for 24 hours survives; South Carolina father charged

author: SMRITI JAIN
description: Inflation was higher in rural areas at 6.63%, while the urban rate was 5.41%. Food inflation, calculated using the All India Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), reached a provisional 8.94% in October 2026 from a year earlier. The corresponding rates were 9.09% in rural areas and 8.68% in urban areas.
title: Retail inflation soars to 2-year high of 6.09%, crosses RBI’s upper limit

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Jamie Dimon, CEO of JPMorgan Chase, expressed concerns about autonomous AI agents managing personal banking transactions. He emphasized that granting these agents access to sensitive banking information poses significant security risks. Dimon noted the uncontrolled potential of rogue AI agents, which could jeopardize consumer accounts and financial integrity. Despite warnings, JPMorgan is working on its proprietary AI tool for managing liquidity.
title: Jamie Dimon warns against letting AI agents make payments for customers

author: PRANAV SHUKLA
description: In a remarkable feat, Kusal Mendis has etched his name in cricket history as the first Sri Lankan to score a century on debut as Test captain, amassing an impressive 117 not out. His stellar performance came at a crucial moment, aiding Sri Lanka in recovering from a challenging position.
title: Kusal Mendis scripts history, joins Kohli, Smith and Root in elite club

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed serious worries about interruptions to the Starshield satellite communication system. He pointed out that speed limitations are obstructing military operations aimed at intercepting Russian drones that are escalating attacks. These issues seem to be systematic rather than just technical glitches. While earlier restrictions were noted in October, the Ukrainian defense ministry has recently reported a resumption of services.
title: 'Not random': Zelenskyy flags 'systematic disruptions' in Musk's Starshield

author: PRIYANKA JAISWAL
title: Netanyahu's Iran gamble: Can caretaker Israeli PM launch a war?

author: RAJIV KUMAR
description: In Begusarai, a 28-year-old woman faced a new attack closely following a gang rape incident. She was thrown from her house roof, reportedly by criminals pressing her family to withdraw the rape case. This incident occurred four months after the brutal gang rape that left her injured and in fear. Despite the arrest of several suspects, threats from the main accused continued against her family.
title: Bihar gangrape survivor thrown off roof; family alleges threats to drop case

author: SIDDHI DHARMADHIKARI
description: A woman selling flowers on a roadside in Hauz Khas was assaulted by multiple men with sticks. Video footage of the incident is currently circulating on social media platforms, showcasing the violent altercation. According to social media claims, the men had allegedly asked her to sell drugs, which she refused. Local police acknowledged they had not received a formal complaint but are currently investigating the incident.
title: Delhi woman selling flowers attacked with sticks by multiple men on camera

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: In Newark, New Jersey, a devastating accident unfolded when a woman was fatally struck by a vehicle. The driver, initially convinced she had only collided with a black garbage bag, proceeded to park her car at a nearby supermarket. It was only after that she discovered the woman trapped under her vehicle. Emergency services arrived promptly, but sadly, the victim was pronounced dead at the scene.
title: Woman killed in New Jersey after driver mistakes her for a garbage bag

author: ARYAN SINGH
description: Residents in Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities are grappling with severe power outages stemming from Russian strikes on vital energy infrastructure. These disruptions leave many without electricity, heating, or running water for prolonged periods. Persistent air raid alerts hinder restoration efforts, leaving families to navigate life in darkness and seek solace in candlelight and board games.
title: Kyiv faces 20-hour blackouts as Russian strikes cripple Ukraine's power grid

author: SANJAY SHARMA
description: Anax Joshi, a Class 10 student from St Mary's High School in Kerala's Idukki district, has won the Bala Shastra Puraskaram for designing a remote-controlled multipurpose agricultural vehicle. His innovation aims to reduce farmers' physical workload and the cost of purchasing separate machines for different farming operations. While the project offers a promising approach to small farmers' challenges, practical field trials will be essential to establish its reliability, affordability and suitability for everyday agricultural use.
title: Kerala Class 10 student builds remote-controlled farm machine, wins science award

author: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA
description: In 2026, the emergence of the PJ.2.1 Covid-19 variant has sparked concern as it rapidly spreads across various nations. Laboratory analyses reveal its enhanced ability to penetrate human cells compared to earlier strains. While it showcases limited evasion of antibodies, its increased affinity for the ACE2 receptor raises alarms over transmissibility. Ongoing surveillance and further studies are crucial to grasp its impact on disease severity and overall public health.
title: New Covid variant spreads from Canada to US, Europe & Asia: What we know about PJ.2.1

author: KARAN MANRAL
title: Chinese vloggers in Dhaka scale back 'anti-India' activities amid increased surveillance

author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
description: The festival calendar also worked in favour of jewellery purchases. Dhanteras was observed on November 6, followed by Diwali on November 8. Both occasions fell in the early part of the month, when salaried employees typically receive their monthly pay and festive bonuses. In the current fiscal year through September, gold sales by volume declined by nearly 50%.
title: Indians buy 52 tonnes of gold as prices fall from Rs 1.8 lakh peak to Rs 1.42 lakh

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Jhon Jairo Velásquez, infamously known as 'Popeye', served as a notorious hitman under drug lord Pablo Escobar, reportedly carrying out over 250 murders, including numerous high-profile hits. After 23 years of incarceration, he turned to social media fame with his YouTube channel 'Repentant Popeye,' where he ruminated on his violent past and critiqued governmental actions. Sadly, he succumbed to oesophageal cancer in 2020 following a short imprisonment.
title: Meet Pablo Escobar's hitman who became a YouTuber after 3,000 killings

author: TOI WORLD DESK
title: Community raises $50,000 for Canadian hockey player, 15, battling rare cancer

author: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI
description: The incident took place at a hotel lobby ahead of an MMA event scheduled in Abu Dhabi this weekend.
title: Slap, punches and chaos: MMA fighter attacked in hotel lobby, video goes viral

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A Virginia appeals court has rejected a couple’s claim for additional compensation over an I-495 highway expansion, ruling that they could seek damages only for the temporary easement taken from their property, not losses linked to the wider road project. Their expert had estimated that the project could reduce the property’s value by nearly $500,000.
title: Virginia couple's $500,000 highway loss claim rejected after $29,700 payout

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: China has firmly dismissed the United States' claims linking Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia, to a Chinese spy, labeling them as unfounded fabrications. Foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning has urged the US to cease its creation of false narratives aimed at justifying a technological blockade. Meanwhile, Nvidia is conducting its own investigation concerning the allegations related to Alice Huang, a businesswoman.
title: 'US fabricating spy narratives to impose tech blockade': China on Nvidia CEO row

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: The Reserve Bank of India is contemplating a ban on private equity firms holding majority stakes in multiple non-banking financial companies. The planned regulations aim to distinguish between controlling stakes and smaller investments, with the latter facing less scrutiny. Growing foreign investment interest in India's financial sector includes significant deals by major firms such as Blackstone and Temasek.
title: RBI plans to ban private equity firms from holding controlling stakes in multiple NBFCs

author: DHRUV YADAV
description: The Royal Navy aims to launch the Talon Blue drone from its aircraft carriers next year. This trial is significant for India's aircraft carrier, INS Vikrant, which also uses ski-jump launches. India's Navy is developing its own Naval Collaborative Combat Air Vehicle to operate alongside existing fighters. Successful tests from British carriers could provide valuable insights for India's naval capabilities.
title: Britain's aircraft carrier drone experiment could hold the key to India's next naval leap

author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
title: Kejriwal, daughter get death threats; Rs 7cr demanded in Bishnoi gang's name

author: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA
description: A Frontier Airlines flight faced a critical situation as a bathroom sink started leaking profusely mid-air. While en route to Detroit, the crew had to make an emergency landing at Chicago O'Hare International Airport. Noticing water flooding the cabin, pilots acted swiftly, concerned about damaging electronics. Footage revealed alarming amounts of water accumulating on the cabin floor, though the aircraft was safely landed without further incident.
title: Bathroom leak floods Frontier flight, forces emergency landing in Chicago

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: Kia India plans to invest $2 billion in a new manufacturing plant in Andhra Pradesh. This expansion aims to create approximately 12,000 jobs and increase annual production capacity to 6.3 lakh vehicles. The company currently operates a plant in Anantapur, which was established in 2017 and has a capacity of 4.30 lakh vehicles. Kia has exported over 4.1 lakh vehicles to nearly 100 countries, reinforcing India's manufacturing capability.
title: Kia to invest $2 bn in new Andhra plant, boost annual car production to 6.3 lakh

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: The SS United States, once the fastest passenger ship, was sunk in the Gulf of Mexico. This project aimed to create the world’s largest artificial reef for marine life. The vessel's sinking took longer than anticipated due to safety measures during the operation. Now resting about 180 feet underwater, the ship will become a diving destination. Previous failed commercial efforts to repurpose the ship prompted its preservation as a reef.
title: From fastest ship to largest artificial reef: US ocean liner sinks off Florida

author: etimes.in
description: In a remarkable feat of innovation, Anax Joshi, a Class 10 student from Idukki, engineered a remote-controlled multipurpose vehicle designed specifically for the agricultural sector. This groundbreaking invention aims to alleviate the burdens of physical labor and significantly reduce the time required for various farming tasks, showcasing a seamless integration of technology in everyday farming, while earning recognition for its potential impact on agricultural efficiency.
title: Kerala Class 10 student builds remote-controlled farm vehicle, wins state award

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: After tying the knot, Shweta Suman returned to her roots in Bihar, where she launched a pioneering technology venture named Swadeza. The company specializes in AI-driven tools designed to enhance the semiconductor design workflow. Swadeza made waves recently by unveiling its innovative platform, FORGE, during SEMICON India 2026 in New Delhi, showcasing the untapped potential of startups in regions outside traditional tech hubs.
title: Shweta Suman returns to Bihar to build AI-powered semiconductor design tools

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Billionaire Ken Griffin's migration from Chicago to Miami marks a significant shift in the financial landscape, as he invests heavily in local infrastructure. Acquiring every residential unit in a downtown high-rise, he's setting up a grand headquarters. His $3 billion pledge towards education and healthcare initiatives promises to uplift communities, though his arrival has stirred controversies over political sway and increasing living expenses.
title: Miami billionaire Ken Griffin buys all 138 apartments in downtown condo

author: PRANJAL PANDEY
description: On Christmas Day in 1978, Sonia Gandhi brought a homemade lunch to Tihar Jail for her mother-in-law. Indira Gandhi, a former Prime Minister, was imprisoned during a turbulent political period. The meal was extended to include prison guards and a fellow inmate related to a notorious killer. Despite resistance, Sonia felt compelled to keep family traditions alive during this difficult time.
title: When Sonia Gandhi carried lunch to Tihar for Charles Sobhraj's accomplice

author: TOI WORLD DESK
title: Roberto Clemente's sons lose Supreme Court appeal in $45m image rights case

author: SMRITI JAIN
description: China and India, Russia's two biggest fossil fuel customers, both recorded their highest monthly purchases since January 2022. The figures underline Moscow's continued reliance on Asian markets, even as Western governments step up restrictions on its energy trade. India was the second-largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels in October 2026.
title: EUR 6.4 billion: India’s crude oil imports from Russia hit record high in October

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Mark Zuckerberg is utilizing his Muse AI agent to improve his family interactions and personal fitness training. He engages his three-year-old daughter in baking activities planned by the agent for their weekends. The agent also assists him in securing mountain climbing permits for adventures with his older daughter. He employs Muse to review footage from his MMA gym training sessions for feedback.
title: Mark Zuckerberg says he uses AI agent to be a better father, better husband

author: SAHIL MALHOTRA
description: Virat Kohli brought match-like intensity to India's training session in Mount Maunganui, turning the nets into a fiercely competitive contest with Arshdeep Singh and Kuldeep Yadav. From animated exchanges and playful banter to sharing bowling insights, the former India captain's refusal to switch off his competitive instinct stood out.
title: Virat Kohli and the art of not ceding an inch

author: ROHITASHWA RANJAN
title: Farooq Abdullah bats for India-Pakistan talks despite twin terror attack

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: A 26-year-old tourist from Greater Noida died after falling while paragliding in the Bir-Billing area. The incident occurred on November 10, with information relayed through the Emergency Response Support System. A 24-year-old woman, the complainant, stated the man fell during the flight. An FIR was registered against the paraglider pilot following the incident. This tragedy follows a previous incident in October, involving a Bulgarian national who died in a crash.
title: Greater Noida tourist dies after falling during paragliding in Himachal's Bir Billing

author: PRIYANKA MUKHERJEE
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended Diwali and Gujarati New Year greetings to Congress leader Sam Pitroda after the latter spoke warmly about their personal equation. The exchange took an amusing turn when an X user asked for festive wishes too, prompting a response from the Prime Minister.
title: Sam Pitroda praises PM Modi, receives Diwali wishes; X user's cheeky request gets a reply

author: SABI HUSSAIN
description: From political assurances in Delhi to a behind-the-scenes campaign that caught her off guard ahead of the Nov 9 SOM elections, how a quiet rebellion has all but derailed the IOA president’s second-term ambitions
title: A week without end for PT Usha: How a rebellion derailed IOA prez's 2nd-term ambitions

author: SANJAY SHARMA
description: Indian scientists have identified a new deep-sea shark species, Echinorhinus roinee, after specimens caught off Kerala were mistakenly classified as Atlantic bramble sharks for decades. Researchers from the Zoological Survey of India and ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute used physical examination and mitochondrial DNA analysis to confirm its distinct Indian Ocean lineage. Growing up to three metres, the Indian Bramble Shark highlights the unexplored diversity of India's deep-sea ecosystem and the importance of accurate species identification for marine conservation.
title: Kerala shark mystery solved: DNA reveals a new species after decades

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: A devastating crash unfolded on Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Road, resulting in numerous casualties and injuries. Swiftly reacting, emergency units from police and ambulance services, along with Civil Defence, rushed to the site. They administered first aid and transported victims to nearby hospitals for essential care. Fujairah Police have initiated an investigation to ascertain the accident's causes, urging the community against spreading false information.
title: Fujairah midnight crash: Several dead after truck hits multiple vehicles

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In the quaint town of Monowi, Nebraska, Elsie Eiler juggles her roles as the mayor and lone resident. Despite the solitude, her tavern serves as a vibrant hub for visitors seeking food, drinks, and companionship, fostering connections that transcend Monowi's unique story. With her unwavering commitment, Elsie not only sustains the town’s essential services but also nurtures the ties to nearby communities, ensuring its enduring legacy.
title: Meet America's only resident of Monowi, who also serves as town mayor

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Roy Sullivan, renowned for enduring seven lightning strikes during his tenure as a park ranger, faced numerous injuries that captured public intrigue. Despite his best efforts to shy away from storms, fate dealt him an unexpected hand until 1977. His extraordinary narrative, largely without eyewitness accounts, invites skepticism. Sullivan passed away in 1983, leaving behind an unparalleled legacy of lightning survival that remains unmatched.
title: US park ranger survived seven lightning strikes between 1942 and 1977

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A Colorado pizza delivery driver caring for her 82-year-old mother has received more than $76,000 through a fundraiser started by a family she once delivered an incorrect order to. Their decision to pray with her was captured on a doorbell camera, and the video later reached millions of viewers.
title: Colorado pizza delivery driver gets over $76,000 after family prays with her

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: The Oklahoma Supreme Court has ruled in favor of a lower court’s decision that addressed a homeowner's unauthorized short-term rental practices. The activities violated community rules enforced by the homeowners’ association, leading to fines of $8,528 and an injunction against such rentals. Testimonies from neighbors highlighted noise issues from large gatherings, leaving the homeowner disheartened and struggling financially after a protracted legal process.
title: Oklahoma man faces $8,528 in HOA penalties; court bans short-term rentals

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Elon Musk responded positively to a suggestion of hiring Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid a scandal. Reports indicate Nvidia's board is contemplating Huang's removal due to personal conduct issues. Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair and was seen with a vice president, which raised concerns. The Nvidia board plans to convene to discuss his future soon. Nvidia has been significantly impacted as its shares dropped following the news.
title: As Nvidia board seems set to fire CEO, Elon Musk may have a job for him

author: SAHIL MALHOTRA
description: India are considering releasing Gurnoor Brar from the ODI squad after Friday's match to bolster their preparations for the upcoming Test series against New Zealand. Meanwhile, Ruturaj Gaikwad is likely to replace Shubman Gill as an opener for the fourth ODI, with Ishan Kishan expected to continue in the middle order.

author: SMRITI JAIN
description: Gold and silver price prediction today: Gold may face resistance at 147,000, being the level of 30-week exponential moving average. A close above it would point to a potential move toward the level of 151,500. The bias should remain bullish while support holds at 137,800.
title: What's the gold and silver price prediction on November 12, 2026?

author: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
description: Seventeen-year-old Indian chess prodigy Md Imran is just one Grandmaster norm away from the coveted title, but a US visa crisis threatens his full scholarship at the University of Texas at Rio Grande Valley. After losing his passport and visas in Slovakia, he faces mounting family debt, bureaucratic hurdles and a January 2027 deadline that could derail his chess and academic dreams.
title: Rs 50 lakh debt, visa nightmare: Indian chess prodigy risks losing US scholarship

author: REEBA ZACHARIAH
description: Tata Investment Corporation has appointed Bahram Vakil as chairman after Noel Tata's retirement on November 11. This decision is part of a broader reshuffle at Tata companies due to retirement guidelines. Vakil's prior role allowed him to transition smoothly into the chairman position, succeeding Noel Tata. T V Narendran will also become chairman of Tata International, furthering leadership changes within the group.
title: Noel Tata passes baton to Bahram Vakil at Tata Investment Corporation

author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
description: US lawmakers have raised national security concerns over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with a woman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence. Congressman Jamie Raskin and Senator Chuck Schumer have questioned the potential Chinese influence, while Nvidia's board has launched an investigation and is reportedly considering Huang's future amid growing controversy.
title: Did China use a 'honeypot' to influence Nvidia CEO? US Congress wants answers

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: Bevon Jacobs achieved remarkable success in the Ford Trophy, scoring 202 not out against Otago. His innings included a record-setting 21 sixes, the highest for a New Zealand batter in List A cricket. Despite Jacobs' effort, Auckland lost the match as Otago successfully chased down the target. Jacobs became only the fourth New Zealand player to score a List A double century.
title: 21 sixes in an innings! New Zealand batter Bevon Jacobs comes close to world record

title: 10 killed as passenger vehicle plunges 500 metres down slope in Nepal

author: SMRITI JAIN
description: The rally has lifted the market’s total value to approximately $5.4 trillion, allowing India to overtake Taiwan. The shift in global investment flows has also set India apart from other markets. While overseas investors are returning to Indian equities, Taiwan recorded its highest-ever foreign fund outflows in October as AI-linked stocks came under a worldwide selloff.
title: India back among world’s top 5 biggest stock markets; value climbs to $5.4 trillion

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: Nvidia's board is reportedly discussing the future of CEO Jensen Huang amid controversy regarding personal relationships. Two internal candidates, Ian Buck and Colette Kress, have emerged for potential succession. A decision on interim leadership is expected soon, with Kress favored for stability and Buck for technical expertise. Several external candidates, including Arm CEO Rene Haas, are also being considered.
title: CFO Colette Kress to engineer Ian Buck - who could succeed Nvidia CEO if he exits?

description: Punch, a Japanese macaque, faced a rough start when he was separated from his mother. He found solace in a stuffed orangutan, which offered him companionship during his early struggles. As time progressed, Punch blossomed and has begun socializing with a younger baby macaque. The zookeepers played a pivotal role in helping him adapt and grow, marking his journey from solitude to engagement within the troop.
title: Rejected by mother and bullied, monkey raised with toy now cares for baby macaque

description: On November 4, a 20-year-old woman was pushed off a local train at Naigaon railway station. She lost her left arm after the incident and is currently receiving treatment. The accused, a 53-year-old man, allegedly molested her before pushing her off the train. He has been arrested after police examined CCTV footage from the station. A case of molestation and attempted murder has been filed against the suspect.

title: Axar Patel reluctant to lead, Delhi Capitals in a fix ahead of IPL auction

author: ISHITA JAIRATH
description: Commuters in Delhi dealing with GRAP restrictions are experiencing higher travel costs and longer commute times. Many are switching from personal vehicles to app-based cabs as an alternative. For instance, daily expenses have significantly increased for several individuals, with some reporting extra monthly costs of up to Rs 30,000. Public transport options like the metro are often not viable due to connectivity issues.
title: GRAP’s commute tax: Longer travel time, bigger hole in Delhiites’ pockets

author: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA
description: Gibran Rakabuming Raka, Indonesia's Vice-President, resigned after challenges regarding his eligibility emerged from court rulings. His resignation was submitted to the People’s Consultative Assembly leadership in Jakarta. This situation arose after the Constitutional Court ruled his education documents were insufficient for election requirements. Raka had communicated his intention to resign to President Prabowo Subianto to avoid further political controversy.
title: Under fire over his degree, Indonesia's VP Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigns

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: At an age when many people slow down, Kamla Negi started a new life, new job and took on one of the toughest jobs in the hills of Uttarakhand. She is 60-years-old and is repairing punctures in scooters and cars. Not only this, she is also handling the massive tyres of trucks, dumpers, buses and JCB machines. The woman belongs from Nainital's Ramgarh region and has built a reputation for doing work traditionally associated with men.
title: Meet Kamla Negi, 60, Nainital's 'Iron Lady' who repairs even JCB tyres

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Violet Jessop's extraordinary journey is marked by her endurance through three catastrophic maritime events. She famously survived the Titanic disaster, which catapulted her into public attention. Even after experiencing the sinking of the HMHS Britannic in World War I, she returned to the sea, defying fear for ocean liners. Jessop's legacy, culminating in her retirement and passing in 1971, remains a testament to her indomitable spirit.
title: Violet Jessop survived Titanic and Britannic sinkings, plus Olympic collision

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In April 1961, surgeon Leonid Rogozov found himself in a dire situation in Antarctica when he developed acute appendicitis. Stranded at a remote Soviet research station, he realized that evacuation was impossible. Demonstrating extraordinary resolve, he performed surgery on himself with local anesthesia, assisted by two colleagues, successfully removing his appendix. This incredible act is celebrated as a significant milestone in the annals of remote medical practice.
title: In 1961, Soviet doctor in Antarctica removed his own appendix in surgery

author: NASEER GANAI
description: Ladakh Police removed climate activist Sonam Wangchuk from a protest site in Leh on Wednesday evening. Wangchuk and local leaders protested against hill council elections set for December 4 due to harsh winter conditions. They argued that approximately 25% of Ladakhis are away from the region during this period. The local administration imposed a ban on protests to maintain public order during the elections.
title: Ladakh protest row: Police remove Sonam Wangchuk from protest site

author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
title: Suspected Pakistani drone recovered near International Border in J&K's Samba

author: TIMESOFINDIA.COM
description: A proposed rule by the Department of Homeland Security could change how H-1B visa extensions are processed. If enforced, it would remove the requirement for USCIS to give deference to previous approvals. This change might lead to an increase in requests for additional evidence during extension reviews. Consequently, it could create uncertainty for workers whose employment status and details remain unchanged.
title: US proposes rule change that could affect thousands of H-1B visa extensions

author: G S DHANUSH AND ABHAY
description: In a tragic incident in Outer Delhi, a four-year-old boy named Imran fell into a deep sewer and was declared missing. His body, unfortunately, was located nearly 20 hours later, about 3.5 km from where he fell. The initial search concentrated on nearby regions, leading to significant recovery delays. Authorities pointed out negligence with the inadequately secured manhole cover, and investigations are currently ongoing to hold responsible parties accountable.
title: Boy, 4, falls into sewer in Delhi’s Ranhola, mutilated body located at water plant

author: NIKHIL SHARMA
description: An altercation between Mohan Sharma and his neighbor Paramjeet Dhankar led to escalating hostility. Sharma, unable to bear the humiliation, decided to murder Dhankar. On November 6, Sharma lured Dhankar downstairs and shot him multiple times. Investigators revealed a history of disputes between the two families over parking and property issues. Sharma has been arrested and is currently in police custody for further interrogation.
title: 'Happy Diwali': Accused shouted after killing ex-Tech Mahindra regional head

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Anirudh Ravichander and Kavya Maran tied the knot in a serene ceremony in Greece, opting for simplicity over tradition by forgoing a priest and Sanskrit chants. Their heartfelt mangalsutra ritual was attended by dignitaries like Rajinikanth and MK Stalin, enhancing its significance. Anirudh's mother dazzled in a saree adorned with Hindu deities, charming many guests.
title: Inside Anirudh Ravichander and Kavya Maran's priest-free traditional wedding

author: PRANJAL PANDEY
description: Amid rising tensions, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's security cabinet has initiated military preparations for a possible strike on Iran. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot advocates for careful judgment from the caretaker administration during this transitional period, emphasizing that military actions should only be executed in the face of direct threats to Israel. He highlights concerns about Netanyahu's decreasing support in the Knesset, which currently stands at just 46 votes.
title: Netanyahu asks military to prepare for Iran 2.0 as opposition demands no strikes before next govt

author: PRANJAL PANDEY
description: Abhishek Banerjee raised concerns about ongoing surveillance by Kolkata Police near his residence. Following a previous attack during his birthday celebrations, he fears another incident may be planned. The temporary shed outside his house was removed by the municipal corporation on police orders. Despite multiple complaints, Banerjee accused the BJP government of failing to take action against the situation.
title: Watch: ‘Illegal’ tin shed removed at TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee's Kalighat residence

author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
title: 'No room for Taiwan independence': Xi doubles down on reunification push

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: According to a recent PGIMER study, a considerable number of adolescents are experiencing digital stress, particularly among younger children between 10 and 13, who reported heightened stress levels compared to teens aged 14 to 16. Social media anxieties surrounding approval and the fear of missing out exacerbates these issues. The investigation encompassed over a thousand students across North India, prompting a call for parental involvement in managing online pressures.
title: Younger teens face more social media stress than older teens, study finds

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: In a groundbreaking discovery, three Sistan sand boas have been identified in Sikar district, Rajasthan, a first for the nation. Researchers pointed out unique characteristics that set this species apart from the Indian red sand boa. Interestingly, these snakes inhabit urban and agricultural regions, deviating from their usual sand dune habitats.
title: Rare Sistan sand boa, known from Iran and Pakistan, documented in India

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Karen Barlow marks the end of a remarkable 27-year journey with the Royal Flying Doctor Service in Australia. Her dedication to providing vital medical assistance to those in isolated regions is commendable. Barlow not only offered solace during treacherous medical flights but also fostered strong connections with families in crisis. Among her memorable moments, she met King Charles and Queen Camilla.
title: Australian nurse retires after 27 years flying to care for remote communities

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang is under fire due to a reported affair with Vice President Kimberly Powell, who has significantly contributed to the company's healthcare operations for nearly two decades. Investigations are ongoing, including Huang's connections to an individual linked to Chinese intelligence. Huang has publicly acknowledged his infidelity, coinciding with a 3% dip in Nvidia's shares amid these troubling developments.
title: Who Is Kimberly Powell, the Nvidia executive linked to CEO Jensen Huang

author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
description: The Assessing Officer (AO) treated both the property investment of Rs 20,23,778 and the cash deposits of Rs 13,04,900 as unexplained. This resulted in additions of Rs 33,28,678, or approximately Rs 33.29 lakh, to the man’s income. The person contested the assessment before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals).
title: Son faced notices over property buy & cash deposits; ITAT accepts mother's gift evidence

author: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
description: Seventeen-year-old Indian chess prodigy Md Imran is just one Grandmaster norm away from the coveted title, but a US visa crisis threatens his full scholarship at the University of Texas at Rio Grande Valley. After losing his passport and visas in Slovakia, he faces mounting family debt, bureaucratic hurdles and a January 2027 deadline that could derail his chess and academic dreams.
title: Rs 50 lakh debt, visa nightmare: Indian chess prodigy risks losing US scholarship

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, WSJ reports, days after backing his leadership. Huang admitted an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive US officials suspect is a Chinese spy, and reportedly had a second relationship with Nvidia healthcare VP Kimberly Powell. The board was set to meet as soon as Wednesday to decide the co-founder’s future, with no clear succession plan in place.
title: Nvidia may fire Jensen Huang over ‘double affair’ with alleged spy and executive

title: Bullet-riddled bodies of 2 missing cops found in J&K's Kishtwar

author: SHILPA PHADNIS
title: Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao's stake worth $703 million

author: SUBODH GHILDIYAL
description: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir recalls the Wembley bout of 1966
title: Sonia Gandhi memoir: 1966 fight between Ali and Cooper that former Cong prez remembers

author: ABHISHEK MISHRA
title: 'Elon, please hire Jensen': Musk responds to X user's request on Nvidia CEO

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: People often engage in strategic eating habits, savoring their favorite bites either at the beginning or the end of a meal. Researchers link this behavior to the thrill of anticipation and the overall dining experience. A study focused on sushi consumption highlighted different preferences, showcasing how psychological factors and cultural backgrounds influence when individuals choose to indulge in their preferred dishes.
title: Why saving the best bite for last says more about you

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: In a significant move, Santosh Janardhan will relinquish his leadership position at Meta by early 2027, paving the way for David Brown, who joined from AWS in July, to take the helm. Janardhan will provide guidance during Brown's transition to ensure a smooth handover. This strategic shift is part of Meta's ongoing effort to enhance its data center operations and bolster investments in artificial intelligence and related infrastructure.
title: Meta’s infrastructure chief Santosh Janardhan quits after 15 years

author: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA
title: Brooklyn building collapse: 2 dead, 10 injured as firefighters search for survivors

author: etimes.in
description: Nitesh Tiwari's film 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' has achieved significant box office success within its first week. The film, featuring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, is close to reaching Rs 1,000 crores worldwide. It collected Rs 934.55 crores globally, with substantial earnings from both domestic and international markets. The Hindi version has dominated the Indian revenue, contributing to a total of Rs 394 crores.
title: 'Ramayana': Ranbir Kapoor, Yash's film nears Rs 1,000 cr

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: Bhavesh Patidar, hailing from a traditional farming lineage, established SolarSure with a vision to support farmers through solar energy initiatives. By equipping over 50,000 farmers with solar installations across various states, the company is creating alternative revenue streams beyond conventional farming. Utilizing advanced technology, SolarSure evaluates land for optimal solar performance, aiming to bolster the financial stability of farming families throughout India.
title: IIT-BHU grad's project helps 50,000 farmers earn from solar power

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: Stuart MacGill has acknowledged using sandpaper on the ball during his cricket career, indicating it was not a deliberate cheating strategy. His admission follows recent statements made by Usman Khawaja in his memoir, which has reopened discussions on Sandpapergate. Cricket Australia maintains that the wider team was unaware of any wrongdoing during the 2018 Cape Town Test.
title: 'I'd tape it to my thumb': Ex-Australia star admits to using sandpaper

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Nvidia's board has launched an inquiry into CEO Jensen Huang following claims of compromising sensitive company information. In a surprising turn, Huang acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, raising national security flags due to her links with Chinese intelligence. Although no current evidence points to jeopardized security, the investigation is set to explore this aspect.
title: Nvidia Board issues another statement, 2 days after saying not 'firing' Jensen Huang

author: PRATYUSH RAJ
description: Punjab Kings co-owner Ness Wadia opens up about the blockbuster Hardik Pandya-Arshdeep Singh trade, admitting that letting go of the India pacer was a difficult decision. Wadia explains the cricketing rationale behind acquiring Pandya, reveals how the negotiations unfolded and outlines the franchise's long-term ambitions of building a championship-winning team.
title: 'We are looking at Hardik Pandya as a long-term investment': Ness Wadia

author: NIKHIL SHARMA
description: CCTV footage captured the events leading to the murder of Paramjeet Dhankhar by his neighbour, Mohan Sharma. An argument lasting four minutes escalated, resulting in Sharma shooting Dhankhar multiple times. Despite attempts to escape, Dhankhar was pursued and fired upon even after collapsing. Investigations indicate a long-standing dispute over parking may have sparked the incident. Sharma was later arrested, with police probing previous disagreements that might have contributed.
title: Chased & then shot: Chilling CCTV video of ex-Tech Mahindra regional head's murder

author: VIVEK DUBEY
title: Jensen Huang had another affair with Nvidia VP who reported to him: Report

author: TNN
description: For the 2025-26 Swachh Survekshan Awards, Navi Mumbai has claimed the esteemed title of the cleanest city. Following closely are Surat and Vijayawada, securing the second and third positions, respectively. Additionally, Rewa from Madhya Pradesh has been honored as the cleanest riverfront town this year. Significant mentions include Rudrapur as the cleanest Himalayan city, along with various award categories highlighting different city populations.
title: Navi Mumbai India's cleanest city, Indore's domination ends

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: Donna Kelce faced the heartbreak of losing her mother early in life, but her stepmother stepped in with love and motivation. This support fueled her journey as a dedicated athlete and a nurturing mother to NFL stars Jason and Travis Kelce. She encouraged them to play a variety of sports and emphasized the importance of commitment. To this day, she delights in reminiscing before their significant games, showing unwavering support.
title: How Donna Kelce's second mother inspired her to raise Jason and Travis Kelce

author: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
description: Australian captain Pat Cummins was spotted having an animated conversation with wife Becky in Sydney, marking his first public appearance since Usman Khawaja reignited the 2018 Sandpaper-gate controversy. Khawaja claimed the entire dressing room knew about the ball-tampering plan, with David Warner backing him. Meanwhile, Khawaja has refused to reveal further details about the bowlers' involvement.
title: Pat Cummins spotted in heated conversation with wife Becky amid Sandpaper controversy

author: TRISHA MAHAJAN
description: Nvidia shares plummeted by 8% in after-hours trading following revelations about CEO Jensen Huang's alleged extramarital affairs, including a controversial link to a businesswoman associated with Chinese intelligence. The company's board is set to convene to deliberate on Huang's fate in light of these serious allegations. An investigation conducted by the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz is currently underway.
title: Nvidia shares fall 8% after hours as board reportedly weighs Jensen Huang's 'exit'

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: Nawazuddin Siddiqui is committed to ensuring that his daughter Shora completes her education before embarking on a career in film. Although she has already performed in theater and received several enticing film offers, he emphasizes the necessity of formal acting training for her growth. To deepen her understanding of cinema, he encourages her to watch films rich in depth.
title: Nawazuddin on daughter Shora's debut: 'Getting offers, but...'

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: Auqib Nabi had a quiet start to the five-match series, returning figures of 0/33 in the first ODI, which India won by five wickets (DLS method). He bounced back in the second match, dismissing New Zealand openers Will Young and Tim Seifert to help India register a four-run victory (DLS method). The third ODI in Hamilton was abandoned due to rain, with India leading the series 2-0.
title: 'Pace is good, but skills matter': Auqib Nabi on adapting to New Zealand conditions

author: VIVEK DUBEY
title: Watch: US war secretary Pete Hegseth reprimanded by soldier at Arlington Cemetary

author: DHANANJAY MAHAPATRA
description: The Supreme Court collegium is working to establish a systematic policy for transferring judges among high courts. Currently, transfers are largely subject to personal criteria, which the collegium aims to revise. This new policy emphasizes objective reasoning to streamline the transfer process, reduce personal biases, and enhance accountability regarding judges’ conduct and expertise, marking a pivotal evolution in judicial integrity management.
title: Judge ‘close to’ CJI runs transfer risk once mentor leaves office

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's plans for a privacy fence at their $5.35 million Ohio mansion are facing fresh scrutiny from a local review board. While some neighbours have raised concerns over landscaping changes, deer safety and a shared sewer line, another resident says most of the Bratenahl community supports the couple and wants them to feel welcome.
title: Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce's $5.35M mansion privacy wall faces review

author: ABHISHEK CHOUDHARI
description: Mohan Bhagwat highlighted the historical significance and environmental benefits of traditional Diwali celebrations during a recent event. He emphasized the need for a scientific understanding to preserve these practices. According to Bhagwat, festivals play an essential role in keeping society vibrant and connected. He expressed the growing global recognition of Diwali, which is now celebrated internationally. Bhagwat urged adherence to societal rules to enhance collective well-being and safety.
title: Once upon a time, crackers purified air, didn’t pollute: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat

author: etimes.in
description: In a surprising turn of events, students from the Allen Career Institute in Kota staged a protest for their missing Diwali sweets. With requests for six promised laddus, the demonstration sparked a social media movement known as the Laddu Janta Party. Although the institute cited logistical challenges, the sweets were eventually distributed following the protests. Meanwhile, rival institutes took advantage by providing their own treats, adding to the overall enthusiasm.
title: Kota students form 'Laddu Janta Party' after promised Diwali sweets go missing

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A Washington appeals court upheld an uncle's ownership of a family home after his nephew, who had lived there rent-free for 14 years and made several improvements, failed to establish adverse possession. The court found insufficient evidence that both owners had withdrawn permission for him to occupy the property, supporting his removal.
title: Nephew lives rent-free for 14 years, claims aunt's house; court backs uncle

author: AADRITA HALDER
title: Trump administration aware of plans to oust Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang: Report

author: AADRITA HALDER
title: Democrat Scott Colom becomes Mississippi's first Black senator since 1874

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: The first photographs of charred wooden fragments reportedly found beneath Turkey's Durupınar Formation have been released, renewing interest in the search for Noah's Ark. Discovered around 30 feet underground, the pieces show markings researchers believe could indicate human workmanship. Four independent laboratories will examine the samples to determine their age, wood type and possible origins.
title: First photos of possible Noah's Ark wood found under Turkey mountain
